newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee holds at highs but spurns NY gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee holds at highs but spurns NY gains.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed mostly lower on the day, content to hold at the day's highs but spurning the bullish gyrations of the New York market, traders said on Thursday.
July arabicas surged early to hit a new life-high of 264.00 cents/lb after technically-driven speculative and local buying triggered buy stops above 262.00.
But London traders said fund players were already sufficiently long in robustas and a move of around $30 would be needed to lure them back into the market.
"It's got to get to $2,150 to break fund buying stops or get down towards $2,000 to bring in a lot of buyers," said one.
"The funds went very long early in the week and people started to panic," he said, explaining why London coffee had backed away off highs on Thursday afternoon despite the surge in New York.
At the close July robustas stood $8 lower at $2,082, with September off $15 at $2,100. Volume amounted to 5,017 lots.
Another trader said New York had rallied on rumours of cold weather moving into Brazil, and although the frost season was approaching there should be no concern as yet.
"It's hard not to gear your position to the upside," he said.
Meteorologists in Brazil said the outlook for an approaching polar air mass remained unchanged, with no frosts forecast for coffee areas.
Early Saturday morning temperatures should fall in Sao Paulo and south Minas Gerais but no frost is forecast.
